note: Narrow CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-01-01T03:53Z. This CME is only seen in STEREO A COR2 for four frames. The later propagation of this CME is missed due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery starting after 2026-01-01T03:48Z There are a couple of potential sources for this CME. The first is an eruption and some associated dimming from AR 14324 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-01-01T01:39Z. The second is associated with a C9.6 class flare from AR 14325 (S10E03) that peaked at 2026-01-01T02:25Z. The flare and associated eruption are best seen in SDO AIA 131. Based on the latitude of the CME, the second source candidate is more likely.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen because this CME is only seen in STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-01-01T06:24Z. This CME is also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is a large filament eruption over the SE quadrant of the Earth-facing disk. The eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 304, and the filament can be seen rising as early as 2026-01-01T04:52Z. There is some brightening on the SE limb in running difference imagery as early as 2026-01-01-T05:36Z (likely associated with brightening from the rising filament itself), but the structure of the CME is not visible in white light imagery until 2026-01-01T06:24Z. There appears to be some deflection slightly to the south later into the propagation of the CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best-fit measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and on the visible location of the filament. There is also a wider, more northern portion that is not visible by the time the CME makes it into SOHO LASCO C3. Because the extra feature is not visible later in SOHO LASCO C3, the bright bulk has been prioritized for the measurement. The extra, wider feature is more prominent in GOES CCOR-1, but it is still not as bright as the main bulk. The approximate longitude of the filament footpoints is around E60 to E80. Since a triangulated measurement cannot be made as there is no STEREO A COR2 imagery for this event, a starting point of E60 was used for this measurement. Because of this, there will inherently be a greater than normal degree of uncertainty associated with this measurement.

note: CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-01-01T13:36Z. The CME is also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, but is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting after 2026-01-01T04:38Z. There is no good source candidate for this feature visible on the Earth-facing disk. This is likely just outflow following CME: 2026-01-01T06:24Z. There is some southward deflection later into the propagation past the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of distinct source candidate and lack of available coronagraph triangulation.

note: CME first seen to the NNE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-01-01T19:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is currently not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap which began at 2026-01-01T04:38Z. The source of this event is a C6.2 flare from AR 14324 (N24E01) seen in SDO AIA 131 peaking at 2026-01-01T17:59Z. A wide region of dimming and field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284, followed by post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 131 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint loop CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-01-01T23:12Z as well as by GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 (after the data gap) in later frames. The source of this event is faint field line movement seen along the NW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-01-01T22:36Z. The source could be Active Region 14317, which is in the process of rotation off the visible Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). The source is behind the NW limb in SDO and this event is covered by an unusually long data gap in STEREO A imagery.

note: Faint CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and CCOR-1. It is partially obscured by pylon in C3. The CME has a somewhat brighter narrow bulk and a very faint very wide (partial halo-like) shock. No clear source was found in EUV imagery but there is some minor movement of field lines well beyond the limb as seen in the W in GOES SUVI 284 after 2026-01-02T16:17Z. Some ejecta can also be seen from beyond the W limb in STA EUVI 304 around 2026-01-02T16:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis of the faint wide shock of this CME with one-coronagraph method (SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs), based on the fit of the partial halo front with coronagraphs. The source is far-sided and the exact longitude is not known.

Preliminary BULK analysis, as a plane-of-sky with SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 only due to the data gap in STEREO A COR2 and STEREO A EUVI starting around 2026-01-02T16:53Z imagery to see and triangulate the far-sided source.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-01-02T16:53Z. The source is likely faintly observed on the NE disk as a slow filament eruption/surface brightening from two nearby areas, which likely created this CME and the following similar CME: 2026-01-02T21:12Z, with difficulty distinguishing the sources due to their proximity and slow nature. The first area observed as surface brightening in SDO AIA 304 is centered around N40E22 and starts erupting around 2026-01-02T17:30Z. The second area observed as a filament, which spanned approximately N50E20 to N45E10, slowly peeling off the disk in SDO AIA 304 starting as early as 2026-01-02T17:52Z. In SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284, both of these eruptions are observed deflecting field lines further to the NW from these areas, with some dimming in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as no STEREO A COR2 imagery is available to triangulate this CME, which is observed deflected NW away from its source on the NE earth-facing disk.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-01-02T16:53Z. The source is likely faintly observed on the NE disk as a slow filament eruption/surface brightening from two nearby areas, which likely created this CME and the preceeding similar CME: 2026-01-02T19:00Z, with difficulty distinguishing the sources due to their proximity and slow nature. The first area observed as surface brightening in SDO AIA 304 is centered around N40E22 and starts erupting around 2026-01-02T17:30Z. The second area observed as a filament, which spanned approximately N50E20 to N45E10, slowly peeling off the disk in SDO AIA 304 starting as early as 2026-01-02T17:52Z. In SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284, both of these eruptions are observed deflecting field lines further to the NW from these areas, with some dimming in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as no STEREO A COR2 imagery is available to triangulate this CME, which is observed deflected NW away from its source on the NE earth-facing disk.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from Active Region 14334 (S18E70) starting around 2026-01-03T07:20Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. An opening of field lines can be observed over the southeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery at this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Jet-like CME seen to the southeast in SOHO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2A associated with a point source eruption near the vicinity of AR 14334 (S15W59) seen best in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-01-04T00:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using SOHO and STEREO A for triangulation of the longitude.

note: Outflow-like CME seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 likely associated with far-sided eruptive activity suggested by the geometry of the CME as observed from STEREO A. May be associated with some rising field lines observed behind the northwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-01-04T04:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Low confidence measurement as the front of the CME is not easily seen in available coronagraph imagery.

note: Faint outflow-like CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO and not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap; a possible source for this coronal mass ejection is eruptive activity just behind the eastern limb with a rising prominence seen best in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-01-04T10:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft plane of sky measurement as the CME is not seen well in STEREO A COR2A imagery.

note: Narrow CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and later in STEREO A COR2A which could be associated with a sympathetic eruption near the eastern limb caused by the prominence behind the eastern limb beginning near 2026-01-04T12:00Z seen best in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation of the CME leading edge to determine longitude.

note: Very faint CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-01-04T21:12Z. This CME fades before exiting the field of view in C2 and is therefore not seen in any other coronagraphs. The source of this event is likely some minor field line movement seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA starting around 2026-01-04T21:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of E90 due to lack of visible coronagraph imagery and source near the limb.

note: Narrow, bright CME seen to the south-southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2A. The likely source is a thin streamer of plasma lifting from near AR 4334 (S17E43) with noticeable southern deflection seen best in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 171 around 2026-01-05T07:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using all available spacecraft out to 12 solar radii which suggests strong southern deflection.

note: Faint CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2A and GOES CCOR-1 possibly associated with a two-part eruption in AR 4334 (S17E43) seen best in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-01-05T08:20Z; while most of the plasma material is directed southward, a portion of the plasma lags behind and is directed to the southeast. May instead be associated with a destabilizing magnetic loop with bright post eruptive arcades high above the AR 4334 (S17E43), but the ejecta does not leave the GOES and SDO EUV field of views until after 09:00Z, suggesting that any such CME associated with the later eruption in AR 4334 is seen after 09:00Z in coronagraph imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A SECCHI COR2A, and GOES CCOR-1 out to about 12 solar radii.

note: CME seen to the southeast in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 but not in SOHO LASCO due to a data gap; the CME is probably associated with destabilizing magnetic loop with bright post eruptive arcades near AR 4334 (S17E43) seen best in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-01-05T08:20Z seen through 2026-01-05T09:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Low confidence leading edge measurement using triangulation between GOES and STEREO A to determine the originating source longitude.

The source of this event is a C2.2 class flare and associated eruption from Active Region 14334 (S15E33) which began at approx. 2026-01-06T00:15Z. This flare is visible in SDO AIA 131, along with dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 and 211. Field line opening can be seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

The likely source of this event is some general field line movement near Active Region 14334 (S15E30) seen in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-01-06T12:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is likely field line movement seen along the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-01-06T11:42Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to source near the limb and lack of STEREO A for triangulation.

note: Narrow CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-01-06T14:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a minor filament eruption seen from near AR 14334 (S15E27) beginning at approx. 2026-01-06T13:31Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a C4.0 flare starting at 2026-01-06T15:43Z from Active Region 14334 (S13E25) as seen in SDO AIA 131. An eruption with dimming and post-eruptive arcades is best seen in SDO AIA 193. This CME likely exhibits deflection within the field of view. A smaller eruption is seen from Active Region 14336 (approximately S09E57) starting around 2026-01-06T15:07Z, but the larger eruption is believed to be the most likely source candidate.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Only one frame of STEREO A COR2 imagery was available for this measurement, so the fit is approximate.

note: CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2026-01-06T18:23Z. The source is likely far-sided, with no clear source on the disk seen in EUV imagery. Field line movement may be seen beyond the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA starting around 2026-01-06T21:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME first seen to the ESE in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-01-07T04:23Z. The exact start time is somewhat unclear due to imagery quality. This CME is also seen in to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The leading edge of the CME is extremely faint and difficult to see in white light imagery. The source of this CME is likely associated with one of a series of eruptions from AR 14334. The eruption beginning around 2026-01-07T03:00Z associated with a C2.9 flare from AR 14334 (S15E18) that peaked at 2026-01-07T03:54Z is the most likely source candidate. The eruptive behavior, including some filamentary structure, and flare can be see across SDO wavelengths but are best seen in SDO AIA 131 and SDO AIA 304. There appears to be some deflection possibly due to the southern extension of coronal hole W of AR 14334 that was centered approximately around S18E05 at the time of the eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 as well as the visible on-disk source location.

note: CME visible to the SE in STEREO A COR2 and the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may be partially obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The likely source is an eruption with dimming seen south of AR 14334, around S30E25, starting around 2026-01-07T03:52Z as best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also seen from the point of view of STEREO A 195, closer to the southeast limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-01-07T06:53Z. This CME is only seen in STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely an eruption from AR 14334 (S15E16) associated with a C7.4 flare that peaked at 2026-01-07T06:12Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131, and the associated eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 193 and SDO AIA 304. There appears to be some deflection possibly due to the southern extension of coronal hole W of AR 14334 that was centered approximately around S18E03 at the time of the eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: This measurement is somewhat subjective because this CME is only visible in STEREO A COR2. The longitude in the measurement is based on the source location on the Earth-facing disk.

note: CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-01-07T10:38Z. This CME is also seen to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. It is partially obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely continuous eruptive activity from AR 14334 (S15E14) that persists for several hours starting as early as 2026-01-07T09:00Z. The ejecta that is most likely associated with this CME is best seen leaving the solar disk in SDO AIA 193 around 2026-01-07T12:07Z. There is some deflection likely due to the proximity to the southern extension of coronal hole W of AR 14334 that was centered approximately around S18E00 at the time of the eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 as well as visible source on the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best f it between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

The source of this event is far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event. However, it is possible this event is associated with former Active Region 14321, which is would have been located roughly around S02E169 at the time of this event.

note: Bright partial halo CME to the S and SE in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs, fnot seen in STEREO A COR2 due to the daily data gap. This eruption starts after ~2026-01-08T16Z to the SE of disk center and is associated with the long-duration C5.6 flare in this active region peaking at 2026-01-08T17:30Z. It is seen in SDO AIA 304/193 as bright, extensive post-eruptive arcades, a large-area dimming, faint EUV wave and erupting filaments seen in 304.

Approximate, one-coronagraph (early SOHO imagery and GOES CCOR-1 imagery) analysis of this CME based on the location of the source location (south of AR 14334).

note: Partial halo CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 at the same time as the more southern CME: 2026-01-08T17:12Z. Alternatively, these two events could be two lobes of the same CME. The source could be the more eastern part of the complex U-shaped filament eruption to the SE of Active Region 14334 (S19E03) (or potentially one of two erupting filaments). This complex eruption starts after ~2026-01-08T16Z to the SE of disk center. It is seen in SDO AIA 304/193 as bright, extensive post-eruptive arcades near the active region, a large-area dimming, and faint EUV wave. Erupting filaments are seen in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate, one-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO) analysis of the eastern lobe of this complex eruption.

This deflection may be due to coronal holes nearby.

cmeAnalyses.note: HIGHLY SPECULATIVE ANALYSIS. Very faint front measured to the N/NW starting with the potential source location and adjusting to fit the front. Deflection highly likely with this event based on dimming seen on solar disk.

note: CME observed to the SE in STEREO A COR2, also observed to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 following a data gap ending at 2026-01-09T04:22Z and in GOES CCOR-1 heavily obscured by the pylon. SWPC_CAT triangulation corroborates this on-disk source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only measurement due to SOHO data gap and GOES CCOR-1 pylon obstruction of the CME, using the observed source centered around S60E20 as a basis. note: Faint CME observed to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and unseen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-01-10T14:53Z. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

The potential source for this flare and CME may be AR 14321, possibly located around S10E115, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2025-12-31, and may be a region of interest seen in NSO/GONG data.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location using GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Faint, fast CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, overlapping heavily with CME 2026-01-11T22:45Z. No discernable source is observed for this CME, but is likely outflow with continued field line movement in SDO AIA 171 following significant O-type CME 2026-01-11T22:45Z, which had a potential source of former AR 14321, possibly located around S10E115, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2025-12-31, and may be a region of interest seen in NSO/GONG data.

note: Bright, wide CME observed to the N in STEREO A COR2, NE in GOES CCOR-1, and NE in running difference imagery in real-time for SOHO LASCO C2/C3 (first observed as early as 2026-01-12T04:48Z, white light not available in real-time). cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as a possible source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

While measurement indicates that this CME is front-sided, there is no definitive source on the Earth-facing disk. A couple of source candidates include some minor field line movement in the far south best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-01-14T13:00Z and an eruption from AR 14336 best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-01-14T16:00Z

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). There are two possible sources on disk, however neither of these sources closely corresponds to the fit.

note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-01-14T16:23Z. The source may be related to an eruption and C3.8 flare from Active Region 14340 (N15E05) starting around 2026-01-14T23:40Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Noting that a coronal hole located southeast of Active Region 14340 may be responsible for northwestern deflection of this CME. The start of the CME is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and after the data gap its front is very fuzzy/faint in COR2 coronagraph. The CME is also partially obscured by the pylon in STEREO LASCO C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Final but somewhat approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the location of the likely source (C-class flare in AR 14340 (N15E05)). The CME is also partially obscured by the pylon in STEREO LASCO C3.

note: Halo CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-01-18T18:09Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 as a halo in later frames. This CME was initially covered by a routine scheduled downlink data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 which began at 2026-01-18T18:00Z but LASCO data became fully available later. The source of this CME is a long duration X1.9 flare from Active Region 14341 (S15E20), which peaked at 2026-01-18T18:09Z, with some possible contribution from Active Region 14345 (S16E27). This flare is visible in SDO AIA 94 and 131 and the associated eruption is seen as a wide region of dimming and field line opening in SDO AIA 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284, as well as very high and large area post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 94, 304 and 193. Ejecta is seen in SDO AIA 193 and in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery (southwardly directed off the SE limb as seen from STEREO A). STEREO A 195 also sees it as a large opening of field lines close to the limb, around the equator.

The filament began to brighten and eject starting around 2026-01-22T01:06Z in SDO AIA 304, spanning approximately N07W12 to S02W03 at this time. Two dimming regions follow this ejecta in SDO AIA 193, one centered around N05E15 (referenced as the source coordinates here) directly after the filament ejecta, and another further away centered around N15E30 starting around 2026-01-22T02:04Z which may be part of this CME front or a following outflow. Wide field line movement deflecting to the NNE in SDO AIA 171 follows this complex eruption.

Starting around 2026-01-23T20:36Z there is a filament eruption with associated moving/opening field lines, EUV wave, and post-eruptive arcades as seen in SDO/AIA 193, 171, 211, 304, and GOES SUVI 284 and 304 imagery. This CME overlaps the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-01-23T17:12Z which is associated with a similar portion of the filament eruption which may have helped trigger this complex eruption associated with this CME.

note: Complex CME consisting of multiple overlapping fronts, the first of which is first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-02-02T00:48Z, as well as in GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The start of this event is covered in STEREO A COR2 by a data gap which began at 2026-02-01T14:53Z and ended at 2026-02-02T03:23Z, but after the data gap at least one lobe of this CME is clearly seen to the ENE in STEREO A COR2 in multiple timestamps. The source of this event is an X8.1 flare from Active Region 14366 (N13E35) that peaked at 2026-02-01T23:57Z and possibly also the following X2.8 flare from the same AR peaking at 2026-02-02T00:36Z. The flares are visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 131. Two eruptions of filament ejecta are also seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with these flares, the earlier ejecta more northwardly directed and seemingly deflecting towards the west, and the ejecta after the second flare which is not as northward as the initial one.

cmeAnalyses.note: Final, approximate and speculative analysis based on the fitting with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) once STEREO A COR2 imagery became available after the end of the daily data gap in STEREO A. This analysis leaves out the earliest, more northward, faint front seen in SOHO C2 and CCOR-1 as the likely corresponding very faint front in the first couple of available STEREO A COR2 after the data gap is very unclear/obscured by brighter following front. The CME is treated as one event in this analysis. The fitting indicates a likely significant deflection westwards from the source location (location of the X-class flares from Active Region 14366), possibly due to the effect of the coronal hole to the NE of the Active Region location. Analysis is complicated by the asymmetrical shape of the CME in STEREO A COR2, the fact that the start of the CME is obscured by the data gap in STEREO and the difficulty separating multiple overlapping fronts in SOHO and CCOR-1.

note: CME/outflow seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and (most clearly) in STEREO A COR2 following and overlapping with CME: 2026-02-02T00:48Z. It is especially distinct in STEREO A COR2, as it seems to have a higher latitude than the CME: 2026-02-02T00:48Z. Its source is not clear but could be the long-duration M5.2 flare from AR 4366 (N13E35) peaking at 2026-02-02T02:51Z as seen in SDO AIA 131.

SHOCK front analysis, of the very faint shock feature observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and even more faintly in STEREO A COR2. This feature is trackable enough in running difference imagery to get a triangulation, but difficult to properly discern the width, so this analysis is presented with some speculation but a good 3D fit between coronagraphs.

This eruption is also seen in STA EUVI 195 starting around 2026-02-15T11:25Z from the vicinity of former AR 14370 (S18W95). Another option is an eruption from an unnumbered region SE of AR 14373 beginning as early as 2026-02-15T07:30Z in SDO AIA 193. cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and it has multiple potential sources, so only plane-of-sky analysis is definitive.

note: CME first seen to the SW partially into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-02-15T12:24Z. This CME is also seen to the SW in GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C3, and STEREO A COR2. This filament eruption can also be seen in STA EUVI 195 starting around 2026-02-15T11:25Z from the vicinity of former AR 14371. The filament and associated, subsequent dimming spans approximately W85 to W100.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen because this feature cannot be triangulated and does not have visible a source candidate.

note: CME first faintly seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-02-16T03:36Z. This CME is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. There is some field line movement near the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-02-15T23:00Z. The start time of the CME is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A EUVI, but some fluctuation of field lines and some brightening can be seen to the far west in STEREO A EUVI 195 when data resumes at 2026-02-16T03:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The leading edge is very faint and difficult to track in SOHO LASCO C2, so only SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 were used for the measurement.

note: Large CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-02-16T04:24Z. This CME is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and as a partial halo in STEREO A COR2 with the bulk to the E. The CME is also seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1, but the majority of its propagation is obscured by Earth-shine. There appears to be some northward deflection very early in the propagation of the CME in the SOHO LASCO C2 FOV. The source of this CME is associated with an occulted M2.4 flare from beyond the E limb (~S10) that peaked at 2026-02-16T04:35Z. The associated eruption and ejecta can be seen across SDO AIA wavelengths, but the flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit of the SHOCK feature in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO C2/C3 measurement based on longitude of previous CME: 2026-02-16T04:24Z.

The source of this CME is most likely an eruption seen near the WSW limb in STA EUVI 195 starting as early as 2026-02-16T09:00Z. The eruption is best seen as some material leaving the disk followed post eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-02-16T13:23Z. This CME is also seen as a faint, partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely a large eruption best seen in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 304 starting around 2026-02-16T12:18Z spanning S30E15 to S10W05. Subsequent dimming and an EUV wave can also be seen in SDO AIA 193, along with a C1.0 flare seen peaking at 2026-02-16T13:07Z in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit of the leading edge in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The CME is best visible in STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-02-16T14:08Z. This CME is also visible as a very faint partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2 following earlier, faster CME: 2026-02-16T13:23Z. The source of this CME is possibly related to the same eruption that resulted in CME: 2026-02-16T13:23Z. The main eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 304 starting around 2026-02-16T12:18Z spanning S30E15 to S10W05. There are a couple of smaller portions of the eruption that could be responsible for this CME. The first is an area of dimming that is deflected slightly to the north best seen in SDO AIA 193. The second is an area of dimming south of AR 14373 that follows the main eruption. It is also best seen in SDO AIA 193. In real time, the original analysis of this CME was complicated by gaps in the SOHO and STEREO A downlink schedules.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary analysis based on best fit between limited frames from SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint, narrow, jet-like CME seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 and in early C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and not visible in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found in EUV imagery, so it is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not seen in STEREO A coronagraph imagery and no source for it has been found in EUV imagery, so only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: Faint jet-like CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and likely mostly obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. STA EUV 304 imagery might indicate that part of the eruption departed the disk later, around 2026-02-17T09:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the approximate location of the source eruption, as seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery and on the fit of this narrow CME in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO coronagraphs.

The source of this event is field line movement seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-02-17T09:55Z, followed by hours of slowly appearing/spreading faint but wide post-eruptive arcades in the SW quarter of SDO AIA imagery, expanding westward from the SE limb and eventually obscuring the NE boundary of the SE part of the large elongated coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

The source of this event is field line opening and breaking seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171/193 beginning at 2026-02-17T17:04Z with full breaking seen at 2026-02-17T18:16Z.

S50E50 in SDO AIA 171/193 beginning at approx. 2026-02-17T23:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

(S07E60) which peaked at 2026-02-18T20:42 as seen in GOES SUVI 131. Field line opening is also visible in GOES SUVI 171 and 193 exhibiting a possible Northern deflection. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: A narrow, faint, fast, jet-like CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2. Covered by the night time data gap in STEREO A. The source is not clear, as there is a lot of activity close/on/behind the SE limb: it could be a minor ejecta close to the SE limb seen after 2026-02-19T18:50Z in SDO AIA 304, although it is too early. There is also a movement/opening of field lines on the SE limb seen in AIA SDO 193/171 after 2026-02-19T20:30Z, following which there is a row of post-eruptive arcades seen very close to the SE limb (S27E80) in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is covered by a night time data gap in STEREO A. The source of this CME is not clear. So only a plane-of-sky analysis with SOHO LASCO imagery is possible.

The source is not visible in STEREO A EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Lightbulb shaped CME seen to the SE in all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). Its source is a large filament eruption centered near S25E60 which begins to erupt around 2026-02-22T15:00Z, as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304, with dimming and post-eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the later timestamps of GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3 coronagraphs and fitting the early timestamps of STEREO A COR2. The CME is seen speeding up in later timestamps.

note: Narrow CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-02-23T05:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a very minor eruption seen at approx. S30E80 in SDO AIA 304 beginning at approx. 2026-02-23T04:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

note: This CME is visible to the west/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2026-02-23T13:38Z. cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. LASCO C3 pylon obscures the front in running difference imagery. The CME front is dimpled and somewhat diffuse, so this analysis encompasses as much of the bright material as possible.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, start time difficult to resolve in LASCO C2 but the CME becomes better defined further into the coronagraphs' field of view. May be faintly visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2, but too faint to resolve well, particularly in running difference imagery. The source is not clearly observed anywhere on disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 only plane-of-sky, as the CME is too faint to resolve in LASCO C2.

note: CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, quickly becomes too faint to clearly see. The source is likely field line movement observed over the equatorial east limb in GOES SUVI 284, starting around 2026-03-06T12:48Z, with a source likely E90-E100.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft analysis of the CME, taken originally as a plane-of-sky at E90, but considered a good approximation of the CME location to simulate. The source longitude could be E90-E100. CME front slightly less than 10 degrees half-width.

note: Faint CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-06T18:12Z. No clear source has been found in EUV imagery for this event, however there is a slow rising and opening of field line loops beyond the E limb, beginning after approximately 2026-03-06T15:48Z, as faintly seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284, possibly indicating a far-sided source behind the limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: This far-sided CME is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and no clear source is seen in EUV imagery. Only a plane-of-sky analysis with SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 imagery is possible. The CME has likely sped up with time, so this analysis is made with later C3 and CCOR-1 imagery, to capture the speed at 21.5 Rs.

note: A clear partial-halo CME seen in STEREO A COR2 to the SW, with the start of the event covered by the nighttime data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. The start of this event is likely much earlier. This CME in STEREO A likely (but not definitively) corresponds to one of several follow-up CMEs to the 2026-03-06T18:12Z CME, possibly to the front that is first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-03-07T00:00Z. The CME is also visible in to the SE in GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very speculative, approximate analysis with two coronagraphs, initially based on the fitting of the clear halo front in STEREO A COR2A and later assuming that one of the less clear follow up fronts in SOHO/CCOR1 is the corresponding front (likely the front first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-03-07T00Z), however this front is more of a speculation. The speeds in analysis can vary depending on the chosen half width, which in this analysis was based on the SOHO LASCO imagery and set to 37 degrees.

note: A faint and narrow CME front seen to the SE in COR2A. The source is likely far-sided, possibly indicated by the minor movement of field lines seen in GOES SUVI 195 on/behind the SE limb after 2026-03-07T09:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: This minor CME is only seen in STEREO A COR2 and not seen in other coronagraphs. The source is likely far-sided, therefore only plane-of-sky analysis is possible for this event.

note: A faint, narrow CME first seen to the SW in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-03-07T13:38Z. It is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 or SOHO LASCO C2/C3. A slow filament eruption on the SW limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting after 2026-03-07T09:30Z (and seen at the same time in STA EUV 304 close to the SW limb) was considered as a source candidate; however, there is too much time between this eruption and the start of the CME for this eruption to be the source. The source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from STEREO A COR2.

note: A loop-like front to the ENE that is originally seen in SOHO LASCO as the southern part of a messy strange front conglomerate (likely two combined fronts). It is not seen in STEREO A because of a nighttime data gap. It is seen the clearest in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is not clear.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is covered by the nighttime data gap in STEREO A and no clear source has been found for it, so it is likely far-sided. Only plane-of-sky analysis with GOES CCOR-1 is possible for this event.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-03-07T14:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1. It is very faintly seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. The front is the more northern portion of a two-part front seen in the NE. The more southern part is evaluated as CME: 2026-03-07T14:30Z. There is no good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-03-7T15:36Z. It is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and dissipates before it reaches the end of the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2. It is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 or SOHO LASCO C3 and is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. There is no independent source signature for the feature. It is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-03-07T14:30Z and CME: 2026-03-07T14:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single coronagraph plane-of-sky measurement using running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2.

note: CME first seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-03-07T17:24Z. It is also seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The front is very slow to start, so analysis is based on the propagation of the CME once it reaches the later frames in the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2. There is no good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. There is some faint, minor, nearly continuous field line movement seen beyond the E limb in SDO AIA 171 for several hours before and after the start of the CME that could be related.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 starting sometime before 2026-03-07T18:54Z. This feature first becomes visible part way into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C3. It is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2. It is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2 and is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. There is not a good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This CME follows a very similar trajectory to earlier CME: 2026-03-07T13:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative plane-of-sky measurement based on limited frames from SOHO LASCO C3.

note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-03-07T23:00Z. It is also seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3. It is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. There is no source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated POS measurement using additional SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 frames.
Preliminary plane-of-sky measurement based on GOES CCOR-1 and early frames from SOHO LASCO C2.

note: Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and N/NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be a narrow moving/opening field lines visible along the NE limb in SDO/AIA 193 and 171 starting around 2026-03-08T09:29Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME first seen to the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-08T14:48Z as well as by STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small area of dimming and field line opening seen beginning at approx. 2026-03-08T13:39Z in SDO AIA 193. This eruption is located at approx. N15E40, but appears to exhibit some Northwestern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-03-08T18:08Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap which began at 2026-03-08T16:12Z. The source of this event is a C2.0 flare and minor eruption seen in SDO AIA 131 and 304 peaking at 2026-03-08T15:07Z. This eruption was followed by a small dimming signature seen located at approx. N05E60 beginning at approx. 2026-03-08T17:04Z as seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2/GOES CCOR-1.

note: This faint CME is visible to the SE in GOES CCOR-1. It is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source of this CME appears to be a filament eruption visible along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 and 284 starting around 2026-03-09T10:44Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky fit using GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a planned data gap. The source for this event is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures observed on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

note: CME first seen to the Southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-10T02:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2026-03-09T13:09Z to 2026-03-10T04:09Z. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen along the SE limb (approx. S25E90) in GOES SUVI 304 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-03-10T01:57Z. A small region of field line opening is seen in association with this eruption in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on the approximate source location.
Plane-of-sky due to source along the limb and lack of STEREO A to triangulate. Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint CME first seen by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-10T04:48Z. This CME fades before exiting the field of view in SOHO LASCO C2 and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a small region of brightening with a small amount of ejecta seen in GOES SUVI 304 located at approx. N25E63 beginning at approx. 2026-03-10T04:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: CME first seen to the NW by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-03-10T10:45Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event was a far sided prominence eruption seen from beyond the NW limb in GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening is also visible in GUES SUVI 195 and 284. This eruption began at approx. 2026-03-10T07:30Z, but did not fully detach from the disk until approx. 2026-03-10T09:57Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME first seen to the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-10T12:24Z. This front fades very quickly and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a C2.4 flare from Active Region 14389 (N13E70) peaking at 2026-03-10T12:04Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, along with field line opening seen in GOES SUVI 193 and 284. It appears that this eruption mostly fails and falls back towards the solar disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: CME observed to the NW in GOES CCOR-1, no observations in real-time due to a STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 data gap. The source for this CME is not directly observed, best observed as field line movement over the far-sided west limb starting around 2026-03-10T21:00Z in GOES SUVI 284. A second front at 2026-03-10T22:45Z in CCOR-1 is likely a slower bulk following an initial faster shock front, though without direct source observations and triangulation this is a somewhat speculative connection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Shock front plane-of-sky with CCOR-1 only, due to unobserved source longitude and lack of STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.
Bulk front plane-of-sky with CCOR-1 only, due to unobserved source longitude and lack of STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery and is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap. The source may be related to an eruption observed on the southwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-03-11T09:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location.

note: CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is a filament eruption centered around S27E57, observed starting around 2026-03-12T13:29Z in GOES SUVI 171/195/283/304 as the filament ejecta, moving field lines, and brightening on disk. Partially overlaps with far-sided CME 2026-03-12T15:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D analysis using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to no available STEREO A COR2 to triangulate, using the on-disk source longitude of E57. With possible deflection, the longitude could range E50-E65.

note: CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 and faintly in GOES CCOR-1, too faint for LASCO C3 and not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely far-sided, observed only in GOES SUVI 284 as field line movement over the east limb starting around 2026-03-12T14:20Z. Partially overlaps with on-disk CME 2026-03-12T14:36Z, and fades after the first few frames in LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky due to no STEREO A COR2 to triangulate, and CME front becoming too faint in C2 past the earliest couple of frames to resolve in other coronagraphs' running difference imagery.

note: CME seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and the southeast in STEREO A COR2. The CME is seen in STEREO A COR2 following a data gap from 2026-03-12T19:39Z to 2026-03-13T04:09Z. The CME is obscured by Earthshine and the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery, but visible in later frames. The source is a filament eruption spanning from approximately S45E30 to S20W30 as seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery with liftoff starting at around 2026-03-13T22:09Z. Dimming is also best seen in GOES SUVI 195 imagery. The eruption is not visible in available STEREO A EUV imagery due to the STEREO A data gap mentioned above.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery as well as the source location in SWPC_CAT. Limited STEREO A images were available for this measurement due to the data gap.

note: CME visible to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME overlaps in the field of view with CME: 2026-03-13T06:48Z in these coronagraphs. The CME is also visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2. There is at least one potential source eruption on the Earth-facing disk as seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 imagery, starting around 2026-03-13T05:44Z as dimming centered around N35W20. Additional dimming can be seen starting around the same time, centered around N25E20, and this is the more likely source candidate.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the source location.

note: CME visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided, and opening field lines can be seen on the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting around 2026-03-13T04:55Z. An associated eruption cannot clearly be seen on-disk in STEREO A EUV imagery, and the west limb of the STEREO-A facing disk is at approximately longitude W143.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Narrow CME visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2. Not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, or STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is an eruption from the vicinity of AR 14392 (approximately S15E60) seen as dimming in GOES SUVI 195 starting at 2026-03-13T09:16Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using SOHO LASCO C2 imagery based on source location.

note: Narrow CME visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is likely far-sided, as moving field lines can be seen beyond the west limb in STEREO A EUV imagery starting at 2026-03-13T13:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Faint and narrow CME first seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-13T17:38Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-03-13T15:09Z. The source of this CME is a small region of dimming and field line movement seen beginning at 2026-03-13T16:24Z located at approx. N45W10 in GOES SUVI 195, but appears to be heavily deflected to the North based on the opening direction of the field lines.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint, narrow CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-13T18:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and partially in GOES CCOR-1, as this CME is partially obscured by the pylon. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-03-13T15:09Z. There is no clear source seen for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of W90 due to lack of discernable source. Measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Faint CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-13T20:48Z but fading before exiting the field-of-view in C2 and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a C8.9 flare from Active Region 14392 (S15E53) which peaks at 2026-03-13T20:23Z. This flare can be seen in GOES SUVI 131, along with dimming and field line features seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source  longitude is unclear, but there is an observed eruption on/around the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-03-14T00:36Z, potentially associated with AR 14384.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2, using limited poor quality COR2 data tracking the faint front edge.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source  longitude is unclear, but there is an eruption observed on/around the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-03-14T05:48Z, potentially associated with AR 14384.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, tracking the full width of the diffuse front as best as possible.

note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and in limited STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption and field line movement from AR 14384 observed on the west limb, around N12W90, in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 starting around 2026-03-14T10:21Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and limited and poor quality STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source longitude could vary E90-E110. The CME shape is quite dimpled, so the best fit here encompasses the full width of the material while the leading most edge is on the southern piece of the fit.

note: The earliest in a series of multiple outflowing extremely narrow fronts seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs to the NNW. Not seen in STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery, which is very sporadic and low quality due to an ongoing campaign. The potential source is a high northern latitude eruption seen in STEREO A EUV 195 starting at 2026-03-14T10:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: One-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO based) analysis of this very narrow jet, based on the possible source (high northern latitude eruption seen in STEREO A EUV 195 after 2026-03-14T10:45Z).

note: Faint CME observed to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, difficult to resolve in STEREO A COR2 due to the faintness. The source is likely a small high southern latitude filament, centered around S62E05, which begins to lift off around 2026-03-14T11:00Z in GOES SUVI 284/304 and was likely responsible for this front and possibly the following CME 2026-03-14T13:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D analysis using the observed latitude around S62 with some minor westward deflection, as the front is not resolvable in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO COR2A for triangulation. Regardless, this CME is likely very far out of the ecliptic.

note: Faint CME observed to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, but difficult to resolve in STEREO A COR2 due to the faintness. The source is likely a small high southern latitude filament, centered around S62E05, which begins to lift off around 2026-03-14T11:00Z in GOES SUVI 284/304 and was likely responsible for this front and possibly the preceding CME 2026-03-13T12:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D analysis using the observed latitude around S62 with some westward deflection, as the front is not resolvable in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO COR2A for triangulation. Regardless, this CME is likely very far out of the ecliptic.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery due to data gaps starting at 2026-03-14T23:15Z and 2026-03-14T12:09Z, respectively. The source is an M1.0 flare and eruption from Active Region 14392 (centered near S15E35) starting around 2026-03-15T09:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Dimming is observed northeast of the eruption site in SDO AIA 195/284 imagery shortly after the flare is observed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: Very faint jet with a fuzzy front seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and in one or two timestamps of C3 running difference imagery. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery due to data gaps starting at 2026-03-14T23:15Z and 2026-03-14T12:09Z, respectively. No clear source has been found for this CME in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in SOHO LASCO imagery because of data gaps in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery and its source is unclear.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in real-time by GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery due to data gaps starting at 2026-03-14T23:15Z and 2026-03-14T12:09Z, respectively. The source is an eruption centered near S12E70 starting around 2026-03-16T09:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: Bright CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-03-16T12:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is an eruption seen from beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 seen beginning at approx. 2026-03-16T11:55Z. This eruption may have originated from far sided former Active Region 14378 (currently located at approx. N17E177). This CME overlaps in the field of view with Earth directed CME: 2026-03-16T13:26Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

note: This CME is visible as a partial halo directed to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-03-14T12:09Z. The source is an M2.7 flare and eruption from Active Region 14392 (S15E19) starting around 2026-03-13T12:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A corresponding EUV wave is observed moving primarily northwest of the eruption site in GOES SUVI 195/304 imagery, with post-eruptive arcades visible starting around 2026-03-16T13:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement following the brightest leading edge portions seen to the north and to the southeast. The measured parameters were based on the source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary as a result.

note: Bright, slow CME first seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-03-16T15:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-03-16T14:53Z. The source of this event is faint dimming and field line movement seen in GOES SUVI 193/284 located at approx. N50W10 beginning at approx. 2026-03-16T14:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location.

There is a bright bulk front and a wider faint shock front seen in all three coronagraphs.

note: Large partial halo CME seen in GOES CCOR-1 with brighter bulk mostly directed to the northwest with wider, fainter shock extending from the north to the southwest starting around 2026-04-01T23:45Z. This is associated with a large-scale, strong filament eruption occurring near N28W25 around 2026-04-01T23:00Z with an associated long-duration C-class flare; the eruption is characterized by destabilizing filament channel starting as early as 22:30Z in SDO AIA 193 followed by a lift off of the filament channel best seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 with bright post eruptive arcades and a broad, large dimming signature seen best in SDO AIA 193. The core prominence structure and the widely opening field lines are also seen very well in GOES SUVI 284.
